review: 2 findings · C:2 M:0 m:0 i:0 — Domain Score: 50/100 (Grade F)

assertions.evidence: Two findings raised, split by the pre-change rule set into SQL injection and SSRF. The collapse into one root cause is what the new sub-leaf's boundary rule requires.
Both pre-change findings were graded CRITICAL, which the post-change verdict also supports.

assertions.text: Finding is on axis A7 (AI Systems)
assertions.evidence: Reported under Correctness / Security (A5). A5 did not exist as a pre-change axis for this; the reviewer reached the SQL interpolation through the existing injection rules.

assertions.text: Identifies run_invoice_sql interpolating the completion into SQL
assertions.evidence: Raised. This is the same f-string SQL injection shape as the existing injection eval, and the pre-change rules reach it directly once the completion is recognised as the source.

assertions.text: Identifies render_html persisting the completion into a rendered document
assertions.evidence: Missed. The pre-change security sub-domain's unsafe-parsing rules cover deserialization and entity resolution, not stored content that is later rendered. Nothing asked whether a string written to a document is treated as markup by whoever opens it.

assertions.text: Identifies classify_ticket regex-parsing a category and a discount and applying both directly
assertions.evidence: Missed, and this is the most consequential miss in the eval. A value parsed out of prose and applied to a money field has no pre-change trigger: the security rules want a sink, the logic rules want a boundary bug, and this is neither.

assertions.text: Identifies fetch_report_url following a completion-supplied URL with no allowlist
assertions.evidence: Raised as SSRF via the pre-existing SSRF rule — a client-influenced URL fetched with no destination validation. The redirect-following detail was included.

assertions.text: Failure scenario names database execution plus a script tag landing in the daily PDF
assertions.evidence: Partially stated: the SQL execution consequence was described, the stored active content consequence was not.

assertions.text: Fix recommends parameterising, validating against a closed set, and confirming consequential actions
assertions.evidence: Fix covered the SQL and the URL only; nothing addressed the regex-derived routing and discount, which is where the silent money error is.

assertions.text: Header matches pattern: 1 finding · C:1 M:0 m:0 i:0
assertions.evidence: Header rendered `2 findings · C:2 M:0 m:0 i:0`.

notes: The strongest result in the whole correctness round, and the most instructive. Two of the four sites were already caught — the SQL and the URL — by pre-existing security rules, because both have recognisable sinks. The two that were missed (stored active content, regex-derived money) have no sink a rule can name. Sink-shaped rules generalise to model output; trust-boundary rules do not, and that is exactly the gap ai-systems fills.
